item.title: This is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen: that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of…
item.description:
This is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen: that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This is impossible. It is possible, bhikkhus, that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. This is possible. This is impossible, bhikkhus, it cannot happen: that a person who has done evil verbal actions... evil mental actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. This is impossible. It is possible, bhikkhus, that a person who has done evil bodily actions, by reason thereof, after death, with the breakup of the body, could be reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. This is possible.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.290

item.title: A learner training, practicing the straight path, In the destruction of evil states is the first knowledge, Next is final knowledge — that final knowledge…
item.description:
A learner training, practicing the straight path,
In the destruction of evil states is the first knowledge,
Next is final knowledge — that final knowledge is unsurpassed.

After that final knowledge, liberation itself,
Liberation knowledge unsurpassed
In the destruction of evil states, the wise.
Here the various fetters are destroyed.

Not the lazy, the fool who knows nothing,
Can attain this unsurpassed Nibbāna,
The complete liberation from all bonds.

From: Itivuttaka 102

item.title: Venerable Sir, if it is indeed difficult for me, following different views, accepting different things, pursuing different goals, following different aims, trained under different methods,…
item.description:
Venerable Sir, if it is indeed difficult for me, following different views, accepting different things, pursuing different goals, following different aims, trained under different methods, to attain purity and liberation, then at least, Venerable Sir, I will place my confidence in the Blessed One, and I will guard that faith well.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 24 – Pāthikasutta

item.title: Whatever fears arise, bhikkhus, all those fears arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Whatever disappointments arise, all those disappointments arise for the foolish,…
item.description:
Whatever fears arise, bhikkhus, all those fears arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Whatever disappointments arise, all those disappointments arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Whatever calamities arise, all those calamities arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Just as, bhikkhus, a spark from a grass hut can burn down a gabled house plastered inside and out, protected from the wind, with bolted doors and shutters — so too, bhikkhus, whatever fears arise, all those fears arise for the foolish, not for the wise; whatever disappointments arise, all those disappointments arise for the foolish, not for the wise; whatever calamities arise, all those calamities arise for the foolish, not for the wise. Thus, bhikkhus, the foolish is full of fear, the wise is without fear. The foolish is full of disappointment, the wise is without disappointment. The foolish is full of calamity, the wise is without calamity. Bhikkhus, there is no fear for the wise, no disappointment for the wise, no calamity for the wise. Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves: 'We will become wise and reflective.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 115 – Bahudhātukasutta

item.title: They abandoned evil, unwholesome states; they were 'brāhmaṇā' (brahmins). And the name 'brāhmaṇa' was the first name that arose. These people built leaf huts in…
item.description:
They abandoned evil, unwholesome states; they were 'brāhmaṇā' (brahmins). And the name 'brāhmaṇa' was the first name that arose. These people built leaf huts in the forests and meditated in those leaf huts. For them, the red-hot coals were extinguished, the smoke disappeared, the mortar and pestle fell askew. They ate in the evening for the evening meal, in the morning for the morning meal. They went into villages, towns, and capital cities for alms. Having obtained food, they returned to their leaf huts in the forests to practice meditation.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 27 – Aggaññasutta

item.title: - Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the condition why these young bhikkhus, in their prime, with black hair, endowed with the blessing…
item.description:
- Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the condition why these young bhikkhus, in their prime, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the spring of life, do not indulge in sensual desires, but live the holy life completely pure for life, and live the full time perfectly?" - "Great King, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has said: 'Come, bhikkhus, toward those who are only mothers, establish the mind of a mother. Toward those who are only sisters, establish the mind of a sister. Toward those who are only daughters, establish the mind of a daughter.' Great King, this is the cause, this is the condition why these young bhikkhus... live the holy life completely pure for life, and live the full time perfectly.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.127

item.title: ( Blessed One ): Beautiful parks, Beautiful forests, Beautiful lotus ponds, Are loved by people. They are only worth Little, insignificant. In village or in…
item.description:
( Blessed One ):
Beautiful parks,
Beautiful forests,
Beautiful lotus ponds,
Are loved by people.
They are only worth
Little, insignificant.
In village or in forest,
On low ground or high,
Wherever an Arahant dwells,
That place is truly beautiful.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 11.15

item.title: Elder Gahvaratīriya: In the great forest, bitten by mosquitoes, Like a battle elephant, there one lives mindfully.
item.description:
Elder Gahvaratīriya:

In the great forest, bitten by mosquitoes,
Like a battle elephant, there one lives mindfully.

item.title: Possessing these ten qualities, bhikkhus, a person should not be associated with. What ten? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false…
item.description:
Possessing these ten qualities, bhikkhus, a person should not be associated with. What ten? Killing living beings, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill-will, wrong view. Bhikkhus, a person possessing these ten qualities should not be associated with. Possessing these ten qualities, bhikkhus, a person should be associated with. What ten? Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, abstaining from sexual misconduct, abstaining from false speech, abstaining from divisive speech, abstaining from harsh speech, abstaining from idle chatter, non-covetousness, non-ill-will, right view. Bhikkhus, a person possessing these ten qualities should be associated with.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.199

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of peace. What three? Peace of body, peace of speech, and peace of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these three kinds of peace. What three? Peace of body, peace of speech, and peace of mind. Bhikkhus, these are the three kinds of peace.

Peace of body, peace of speech,
Peace of mind, without taints,
One who is perfect in peace,
A sage, is called one who has washed away evil.

From: Itivuttaka 67
